name: Ring gaskets, types R, RX, and BX
function: The metal sealing rings that seat in the grooves of API 6A flanges and studded connections; type R and RX for 6B flanges, type BX for 6BX flanges.

tabs.overview: Type R gaskets are oval or octagonal section rings that seal by being compressed in the groove. Type RX and BX are pressure-energized: the ring is slightly larger than the groove pitch so that internal pressure pushes it harder against the groove wall. BX gaskets have a small pressure-passage hole so pressure reaches the inside of the ring. Gaskets are used once; a ring that has been made up is replaced.
tabs.engineering: Material is soft iron or low-carbon steel for standard service and stainless or nickel alloy for corrosive service, always softer than the flange. Gasket numbers (for example BX-169 for 7-1/16 in. 10K and above; verify) map to flange size and rating in the API 6A tables.
tabs.connections: Every ring-joint connection in this system.
tabs.safety: A reused, nicked, or wrong-number gasket is the most common cause of a failed stack test. Grooves are cleaned and inspected before every make-up.

hazards.control: Pressure test before pumping; bleed down and verify zero before breaking any connection.
